name: Fabs & the chip supply chain
summary: Advanced AI chips depend on a handful of highly specialised factories, tools and materials.

text: Chips are made in special factories called fabs, which are cleaner than a hospital. Only a few places in the world can make the most advanced chips.
It's like a recipe that needs a special oven that only a few bakeries own.
D1.analogy: A special oven that only a few bakeries have.

text: Making an AI accelerator involves chip design, fabrication at a foundry, advanced packaging that places memory right next to the processor, and testing.
Each step relies on specialised equipment and suppliers, and several steps are concentrated in a small number of companies and countries.
That concentration is why chip supply shows up in trade policy and export controls.
D2.analogy: Like a relay race where some legs can only be run by one or two athletes in the world.
D2.analogyBreaks: In a relay a missing runner can be replaced by a slower one. In chip-making some steps have no practical substitute at all in the short term.

predict.question: Why can advanced packaging become a bottleneck even when enough chips have been fabricated?
options: Memory must be joined to the processor using specialised processes with limited capacity
predict.explanation: AI accelerators place high-bandwidth memory beside the processor using advanced packaging lines, whose capacity is limited and separate from wafer fabrication.

text: Open problems: spreading advanced manufacturing across more regions, the pace of new process generations, and how export controls reshape who can build frontier systems.
